name: Cettiidae
description: Cettiidae is a family of small, plain-colored bush warblers found primarily in Asia. They are secretive birds that inhabit dense undergrowth and are more often heard than seen.

children.name: Abroscopus
children.description: A genus of tiny, colorful warblers with distinctive face patterns, found in Asian forests.

children.name: Abroscopus albogularis
children.description:
The rufous-faced warbler (Abroscopus albogularis) is a species of the bush warbler family, Cettiidae. It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest.

children.name: Abroscopus schisticeps
children.description:
The black-faced warbler (Abroscopus schisticeps) is a species of bush warbler (family Cettiidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest and scrub, occurring at altitudes from 1,500–2,700 m, occasionally down to 600 m, and is non-migratory.

children.name: Abroscopus superciliaris
children.description:
The yellow-bellied warbler (Abroscopus superciliaris) is a species of bush warbler (family Cettiidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are temperate forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Cettia
children.description: Cettia — a genus of cettia bush warblers in the family Cettiidae.

children.name: Cettia brunnifrons
children.description: The grey-sided bush warbler is a species of bush warbler. It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.

children.name: Cettia cetti
children.description: Cetti's warbler is a small, brown warbler in the family Cettiidae, which breeds in southern and western Europe, northwest Africa and the east Palearctic as far as Afghanistan and northwest Pakistan. The sexes are alike. The bird is named after the 18th-century Italian zoologist, Francesco Cetti.

children.name: Cettia major
children.description: The chestnut-crowned bush warbler is a species of warbler found in South Asia. Although overall population size has not been quantified, this is one of the species that is declining due to habitat destruction. Although its population trend is observed to be decreasing, its decline is not happening in rapid fashion.

children.name: Horornis
children.description: A genus of medium-sized bush warblers with strong legs and unstreaked plumage, found across Asia and Oceania.

children.name: Horornis acanthizoides
children.description:
The yellow-bellied bush warbler (Horornis acanthizoides), also known as the yellowish-bellied bush warbler, is a species of bush warbler in the family Cettiidae. It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
It is found on mainland China and Taiwan. Hume's bush warbler was formerly considered conspecific.

children.name: Horornis anurus
children.description: A bush warbler found in the eastern Himalayas and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Horornis brunnescens
children.description:
Hume's bush warbler (Horornis brunnescens) is a species of bush warbler (family Cettiidae). It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
It is found in the Himalayas of Nepal and India.

children.name: Horornis canturians
children.description:
The Manchurian bush warbler (Horornis canturians), also known as Korean bush warbler, is a bird in the family Cettiidae. The species was first described by Robert Swinhoe in 1860. It is found and known to breed in northeastern China.
The estimated distribution size is reported to be a large range – approximately. Although the global population has not been measured, the population trend appears to be stable. Because of this, the Manchurian bush warbler is evaluated as a least concern species.

children.name: Horornis diphone
children.description: Horornis diphone (Japanese Bush Warbler) is a bush warblers species found in Asia region.

children.name: Horornis flavolivaceus
children.description:
The aberrant bush warbler (Horornis flavolivaceus) is a species in the bush warbler family, Cettiidae. It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
It is found in central and southern China, and the northern extremes of Myanmar and Vietnam. It occurs in the countries of Bhutan, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Philippines, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam and also may occur in northeastern and southeastern Bangladesh.

children.name: Horornis fortipes
children.description: The brown-flanked bush warbler (Horornis fortipes), also known as the brownish-flanked bush warbler, is a species of bush-warbler of the family Cettiidae. It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage. It is found in Himalayas, South China and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Horornis hadrophyllus
children.description: A bush warbler endemic to the Philippines.

children.name: Horornis parens
children.description: The shade bush warbler or shade warbler (Horornis parens) is a species of bird in the family Cettiidae. It is found only in Solomon Islands, where it is endemic to the island of Makira (formerly San Cristobal Island). Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forests and tropical moist montane forests above 600m. It feeds on insects in the undergrowth and on the ground. It has short wings and tail with long yellow-brown legs and slender bill. Its back and crown are dark brown with a dull cinnamon coloured chest and throat. The males and females are similar, although the female is smaller at 14g compared to the heavier male at 18-19g, and may have a browner throat and less warm brown forecrown. The juvenile has a bright olive-yellow chin and throat, greyish front, olive-brown upperparts and a dark crown.

children.name: Horornis seebohmi
children.description: The Philippine bush warbler, also known as the Luzon bush warbler, is a species of bird in the family Cettiidae. It was formerly conspecific with the Japanese bush warbler. It is found only in the Philippines in the Cordillera Mountain Range of northern Luzon.

children.name: Horornis vulcanius
children.description:
The aberrant bush warbler (Horornis flavolivaceus) is a species in the bush warbler family, Cettiidae. It was formerly included in the "Old World warbler" assemblage.
It is found in central and southern China, and the northern extremes of Myanmar and Vietnam. It occurs in the countries of Bhutan, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Philippines, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam and also may occur in northeastern and southeastern Bangladesh.

children.description: The chestnut-headed tesia (Cettia castaneocoronata) is a small insectivorous songbird formerly of the "Old World warbler" family but nowadays placed in the bush warbler family (Cettiidae).

children.name: Tesia olivea

The slaty-bellied tesia (Tesia olivea) is a species of warbler in the family Cettiidae.
It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
